request.title: Cataclysm 0.4 — Lite player interface
request.prompt: UI-ONLY follow-up to accepted Cataclysm build 42147234285-1. User wants LITE games: clean, focused playable experience, while ALL studio documentation, agents, devlogs and source history live only on the BoRHeZ Games dashboard at ../games/. Edit ONLY Cataclysm HTML/CSS and the minimal JS needed to remove obsolete UI. Make the header's existing back anchor a real navigation link to ../games/ labeled '← All games' or '← Arcade', with accessible touch target, not ./ (which currently loops to the current game). Title should read Cataclysm 0.4 rather than stale 0.3 (latest gameplay update already added new enemies/abilities), with the existing one-line subtitle; keep technical build-version element intact for stamper/QA. REMOVE the entire three-tab strip (GAME, AI FACTORY, DEV NOTES), the obsolete factory-tab/notes-tab sections and old council cards, and all related tab navigation and loadCouncil JS/CSS. Don't call /factory-report.json. The game occupies the page directly: title, subtitle, small score/HUD (time, fish, kills, HP), the playable canvas with existing overlays and upgrade choices, and compact controls (sound on/off and restart, pause in-game). Preserve id=best ONCE, but move its existing best-score display from the Start overlay into a small always-visible personal-best line/score strip so it remains visible while playing. This is a local-device best score, not a global leaderboard; label accordingly. Keep keyboard/touch controls and simple help text; avoid extra panels, animations, dependencies, network requests, new mechanics, or sound sliders. Do not change the combat/enemy/upgrade/economy logic or health behavior. Preserve the existing start, pause, resume, restart, game-over, upgrade freeze, score saving and muted audio. Do not edit studio workflows/tests/publisher/other games. Add accessible labels/aria-pressed for mute if helpful. Maintain the game diagnostics contract, #play/#pause/#restart, #canvas, #build-version and boot/version handshake, so trusted touch acceptance passes. Include smoke checks that no tab/factory/notes remnants exist in HTML/JS and that best score updates on game over. Coder report should explain exact UI diffs, not invent gameplay improvements. Deliver only after normal independent acceptance+QA and hashed live verification. Future studios will inherit this minimal game-page design: dashboard is documentation/control, individual games are gameplay.
acceptance: The game page has a working prominent link to ../games/ with accessible visible 'Arcade' or 'All games' label; no link points to ./ for back navigation.
No Game/AI Factory/Dev Notes tabs remain; no factory or devlog content or dead UI code remains, and Cataclysm gameplay is visible immediately below title, subtitle and a minimal HUD.
Cataclysm's visible heading is updated from stale 0.3 to 0.4; build-version element and publisher run-ID stamping remain intact, including boot/version agreement.
Best score is an always-visible small personal-best value, not a global leaderboard, with exactly one id=best and a value that stays correct after game over, restart and local storage errors.
Only essential controls remain: touch/keyboard movement, auto-fire, in-arena pause, restart, simple sound on/off toggle; no settings complexity or additional network dependency.
Preserve all existing Cataclysm gameplay: fish, HP, new variant enemies, three/special level-up options, health milestones, pickup effects, pause/resume and save-best; no mechanics changes.
Page is mobile-first and stays within 360px/390px viewports with no horizontal overflow or obstructive HUD; good touch targets and readable controls.
Existing Playwright touch-start/actor-movement/pointer-cancel/pause/resume/restart tests pass at 360x780 and 390x844 with zero JS/page resource errors.

Coder must run Node syntax check and focused static checks of removed elements and best score. Independent QA must approve and the publisher verify exact live file hashes; no claim of physical Samsung testing.

producer.claim: This job scopes the Cataclysm 0.4 Lite player interface update to deliver a minimal, clean, and fully playable web page UI removing obsolete tabs and content, revising layout and labels, and preserving all core gameplay and controls as per prompt.
producer.rationale: The job requirements explicitly specify only UI modifications (HTML, CSS, minimal JS) to remove the factory and dev notes tabs and content, remove council cards, change the header back anchor link target and label, update game title version from 0.3 to 0.4, relocate and persist the best score display in a small always-visible personal-best strip labeled accordingly, retain existing playable canvas and overlays, maintain existing core gameplay mechanics with pause, restart, mute, keyboard/touch controls and help text, preserve diagnostics contract, and ensure mobile-first layout under 360/390 px width. The prompt forbids changes to combat mechanics, enemy behavior, upgrade logic, health, sound sliders, or addition of new panels or tabs. The final page must show only the game content below header and subtitle with a compact HUD showing time, fish, kills, HP, the playable canvas and overlays, and minimal controls (sound toggle, restart, pause) all with accessible labels. The back anchor must link to ../games/ with correct text and accessible target. The obsolete tabs and their JS/CSS must be fully removed. The best score is local only and displayed once with correct updates after game over and restart. The job demands independent acceptance and live file hash verification before delivery.
producer.objections: Uncertainty remains about compatibility and layout on all mobile devices beyond viewport size constraints. Accessibility label coverage for mute toggle and other controls may require verification. Removing entire JS/CSS code related to factory, notes, tabs, and council cards risks regression or script errors if any dependencies remain. The prompt forbids network requests for factory-report.json but codebase has such calls that must be carefully removed without breaking the rest of the game. The best-score persistence relies on localStorage, which may fail or be absent on some platforms. Independent QA acceptance and publisher hash verification are future steps outside this job.

designer.rationale: The core gameplay loop involves player movement controlled by dragging anywhere on the canvas with one finger, which updates player velocity proportionally within limits. The cat fires automatically at the nearest enemy, and enemies spawn and behave with distinct variants and scaling difficulty. Upgrades are offered on level-up, with a freeze in gameplay to select from visible upgrade choices. The joystick overlay's dynamic positioning might interfere with some edge cases in touch input and might be less discoverable on some devices. No new mechanics or complicated controls are introduced, limiting gameplay variety. The simplified UI may disappoint some players expecting more onboarding information or visual guidance.

critic.claim: The planned Cataclysm 0.4 Lite UI update risks mobile input and user experience failures including unresponsive start buttons, fake progress illusions, deficient touch input handling, improper pause/resume state recovery, viewport overflow, UI balance issues, and missing prompt compliance for prompt-required persistent best-score display and accessible labels.
critic.rationale: Although the evidence documents robust desktop Chromium emulated tests and well-structured game logic preserving core gameplay and upgrade mechanics, it lacks direct physical-device verification, notably on Samsung Android where prior failures were reported. The boot/version handshake error handling depends on timeout visibility but can yield user confusion if start remains disabled without tangible feedback, potentially causing an 'unresponsive start' failure mode. The best score visibility moved from the start overlay to a HUD strip could suffer from UI overcrowding, risking 'balance' issues impacting readability or occlusion on narrow 360/390px viewports, especially on low-end devices with localStorage failure risks unverified in-field. Touch input is mainly handled via pointer events with fallback for Samsung Android's quirks; yet environmental diversity leaves uncertain if all pointercancel, touchcancel, and pointer loss scenarios are robustly covered without dangling input states or joystick overlay misplacements causing 'touch input' failures. Pause/resume mechanisms rely on game.mode strings and input clearing, but asynchronous events like visibility changes or pointercancel might yield inconsistent state resumption or stuck freeze states ('pause/restart' risk). The prompt mandates no horizontal overflow below 390px, but responsive CSS adjustments contingent on varied device metrics remain uncertain due to no live multi-device snapshot evidence. The removal of tabs and factory report code is planned to minimize UI clutter, yet the complexity of this code and CSS selectors risk partial leftovers causing invisible DOM or script errors. Aria-labels and aria-pressed attributes on the mute toggle are suggested but not evidenced as fully tested for all accessibility scenarios. Finally, the prompt requires a single #best element always visible with correct updates post-gameover, restart, and localStorage errors—this must be concretely verified in integration tests to avoid 'missing prompt requirements' failures.
critic.objections: The existing tests and QA claims note passing desktop emulated mobile viewports with no JS errors or resource misses, including upgrade mechanics freezing correctly, valid HUD updates, and sound toggle functionality with accessibility hints. Independent AI QA and publisher hash verification are pending and out of scope for now but might reveal residual bugs. The code handles Samsung Android shims cautiously for pointer/touch mismatches, and most prompt criteria are met functionally. However, absence of real device tests, comprehensive accessibility audits, and live multi-device layout screenshots injects uncertainty that must be resolved before final production signoff. Relying solely on synthetic or emulated testing may miss live device edge cases, particularly with unstable localStorage or pointer event behaviors.
critic.proposed_action: Implement comprehensive physical device testing on a wide range of mobile devices including Samsung Android phones, to verify start button responsiveness, genuine game progress (no fake or frozen timers), flawless and glitch-free pointer and touch input including pointercancel and touchcancel edge cases, pause and resume stability from diverse input triggers and visibility changes, and confirm no horizontal overflow or UI obstruction below 360px and 390px widths. Enhance in-page diagnostics and user feedback to guarantee clear recovery messages for disabled start or load failures. Add automated accessibility tests to verify aria-label and aria-pressed states for mute and other controls. Perform static and runtime audits to ensure all obsolete tab, factory, notes and council report code/snippets are fully excised without residual script side-effects. Verify that the single #best score element updates accurately after game over, restart, and in localStorage failure scenarios without causing UI glitches or crashes. Run focused integrated smoke tests simulating long user sessions, pause/resume cycles, pointer cancellations, and upgrade selections to catch regressions. Capture diverse viewport screenshots and video recordings on real handsets. Await independent QA acceptance and publisher hash verification before final delivery.

coder_report:
# Cataclysm 0.4 Lite UI implementation

Implemented the UI-only update in `docs/preview/index.html`, `game.css`, and `game.js`. No gameplay configuration, metadata, tests, workflows, publishing code, dependencies, or other games were edited.

## Exact UI changes
